chunks: 2672 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
“There is no harm in smelling idhkhir, qaysūm, khuzāmā, shīḥ, and similar plants while you are in ihram.”
And ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated, saying:
I asked Ibn Abī ʿUmayr about apples, citrons, lote fruit, and that whose scent is pleasant, so he said: You refrain from smelling it and eating it, and he did not narrate anything about it.

key_terms.التُّفَّاحِ: Apples, cited among fragrant fruits under discussion.
key_terms.النَّبِقِ: Lote fruit mentioned among scented fruits.
key_terms.الْأُتْرُجِّ: Citrons, fragrant fruit mentioned in the ruling.
key_terms.الْإِذْخِرَ: Idhkhir, a type of aromatic grass mentioned as permissible to smell.
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah.

ai.seo_question: What fragrances and scented fruits are permissible or impermissible for a muhrim in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings for the muhrim regarding smelling fragrant plants and fruits during ihram. It indicates that some wild aromatic plants may be smelled without harm, while fragrant fruits such as apples, citrons, and lote fruit are to be avoided in smelling and eating according to the cited report.
